data.body:
OBSERVATION
The installed GC script `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/rebar-worktree-gc.sh` acquires an atomic directory lock at lines 70-75 (`mkdir "$LOCK"`; `trap 'rmdir "$LOCK" ...' EXIT`) before scanning worktrees. Inside the sweep it runs `dirty="$(git -C "$WT" status --porcelain ... )"` at lines 188-190 with no wall-clock bound. If that `git status` blocks, the lock remains held, and the only behavior on a later run is `SKIP: another gc run in progress`. If the process dies without running the EXIT trap (e.g. SIGKILL), the lock directory has no holder metadata and remains indistinguishable from a live holder. The idle test later uses `find "$WT" -type f ... -mmin` without excluding `.rebar/usage.jsonl` or `src/rebar/_build_info.py`, so rebar's own generated files can keep a worktree classified active.

HYPOTHESIS
The outage is caused by doing an unbounded potentially-blocking filesystem/git probe inside a single-flight lock whose state is just a directory. A transient IO stall becomes a permanent service outage because the lock serializes the whole GC and has no timeout, heartbeat, PID, or stale-holder recovery. The misleading `launchctl` surface then hides the outage because a still-running PID plus exit-code column `0` looks healthy unless elapsed time/last-run stamp are checked.

CONFIRMATION
I ran a bounded scratch reproduction of the locking mechanism: one process did `mkdir lock; trap rmdir EXIT; sleep 30` under `perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 8 ...` to stand in for blocked `git status`; a second acquisition attempt while it slept failed and printed the equivalent of `SKIP`. I then created a dead-holder lock directory with no process and confirmed a subsequent `mkdir` still failed, proving the current lock shape cannot distinguish live vs stale. This would have been disproven if the second run could proceed independently or if stale directory locks carried enough holder state to self-recover.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION
Bound each per-worktree `git status` (macOS-safe `perl alarm`/available bounder) and classify timeout as `unknown -> KEEP`. Replace bare mkdir locks with PID/heartbeat metadata plus live-holder and stale-holder branches, and clean up on EXIT/TERM. Exclude known generated noise from the idle mtime scan, and surface stale last-run/overlong active-run status somewhere other than `ps`.
